beats.say: Open playfully: there is a pattern that makes times-ten and times-hundred almost magic. Say we will find out why it works, not just what to do. Colours: pink tens, yellow ones, blue hundreds, green thousands. No questions.

lines.say: Look at this: thirty-four times ten is three hundred and forty. Now a lot of people say, oh, you just stick a zero on the end. That works, but today I want you to know why it works, so it never lets you down.

beats.say: Place value columns H T U. Put 34 in tens and ones, then ×10 shifts every digit one place left, and the empty ones place is filled with a zero. Mark the digits in place. No questions.

lines.say: Here's thirty-four. The 3 is in the tens place and the 4 is in the ones place.
Pink for the tens digit, yellow for the ones.
Multiplying by ten makes a number ten times bigger. And every digit's value becomes ten times bigger, so every digit moves one place to the left.
The 3 was three tens, now it's three hundreds. The 4 was four ones, now it's four tens.
That leaves the ones place empty, and an empty place must be held by a zero. So thirty-four times ten is three hundred and forty. The zero isn't magic: it's just holding the ones place open.

beats.say: Times 100: every digit moves TWO places left, zeros fill the tens and ones. 34 x 100 = 3400. No questions.

lines.say: Now times a hundred. A hundred is ten times ten, so the digits jump twice.
The 3 climbs from tens to thousands, and the 4 climbs from ones to hundreds. Two places each.
Two empty places are left behind, the tens and the ones, so we fill both with zeros: three thousand four hundred.

beats.say: A friend thinks 'times 10' means 'add 10'. Test it with 34. Detective tone. No questions.

lines.say: A friend of mine says times ten just means plus ten, so thirty-four times ten is forty-four. Let's test that.

lines.text: 10 groups of 34 is far more than 44
lines.say: Ten times thirty-four means ten groups of thirty-four. Even ten groups of thirty would already be three hundred. So forty-four is way too small.

lines.text: × 10 = ten TIMES bigger, not ten MORE
lines.say: Times ten makes it ten times as big, not ten more. Big difference!

beats.say: Dividing by 10 and 100 is the opposite: digits move RIGHT. 560 / 10 = 56; 4500 / 100 = 45. The zeros drop off the end. No questions.

lines.say: Dividing is the opposite of multiplying, so the digits go the opposite way: to the right. Two to try: five hundred and sixty divided by ten, and then four thousand five hundred divided by a hundred. Ten first.
The 5 drops from hundreds to tens, and the 6 drops from tens to ones. The zero slides off the end.
So the answer is fifty-six.
For a hundred, the digits move two places right. Four thousand five hundred divided by a hundred is forty-five.

beats.say: State the pattern in one line and show the check that they undo each other: 56 x 10 = 560. No questions.

lines.text: ×10: digits move 1 place LEFT.  ×100: 2 places LEFT.  (56 → 560)
lines.say: Multiplying by ten, digits move one place left. By a hundred, two places left.

lines.text: ÷10: digits move 1 place RIGHT.  ÷100: 2 places RIGHT.
lines.say: Dividing by ten, one place right. By a hundred, two places right.
They undo each other. Multiply and divide by the same number and you land back where you started.

beats.say: Do one TOGETHER, 27 x 10 and 27 x 100. Questions written on the board first.

lines.say: Now you help me. We'll take twenty-seven, and multiply it by ten and then by a hundred.
Digits move one place left, zero in the ones place: two hundred and seventy.

ask.prompt: What is 27 × 10? Tell me where the digits move.
ask.onMiss: Ask: the 2 is in the tens place. Which place does it move to?

lines.say: Two places left this time, with two zeros: two thousand seven hundred.

ask.onMiss: Ask: how many places do the digits move for a hundred?

beats.say: The child works alone: 600 / 10, 7300 / 100, then why the digits move. Hints only if stuck.

lines.say: Your turn to lead. Two divisions to do.
First, six hundred divided by ten.

ask.onMiss: Ask: do the digits move left or right when we divide? By how many places?

lines.say: Now seven thousand three hundred divided by a hundred.

ask.onMiss: Ask: the digits move two places right. Where do the 7 and the 3 end up?

lines.text: Each digit becomes 10 times bigger/smaller, so it moves one place
lines.say: The pattern works because every digit becomes ten times bigger, or smaller, which is exactly one place.

ask.prompt: In your own words: why do the digits move when we multiply by 10?
ask.lookFor: Each digit becomes 10 times bigger, so it moves up one place value.
ask.onMiss: Ask: three tens times ten is how many? Which place is that?
